arxiv-2008-07013.title: Evidence for electroweak production of four charged leptons and two jets in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2008-07013.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by . Evidence is presented for the electroweak (EW) production of two jets (jj) in association with two \PZ bosons and constraints on anomalous quartic gauge couplings are set. The analysis is based on a data sample of proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV collected with the CMS detector in 2016–2018, and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 137 \fbinv .

arxiv-2010-05023.title: Cuvée : Blending SMT-LIB with Programs and Weakest Preconditions
arxiv-2010-05023.creator: Gidon Ernst
arxiv-2010-05023.description: Abstract Cuvée is a program verification tool that reads SMT-LIB-like input files where terms may additionally contain weakest precondition operators over abstract programs. Cuvée translates such inputs into first-order SMT-LIB by symbolically executing these programs. The input format used by Cuvée is intended to achieve a similar unification of tools for that for example synthesize loop summaries.

arxiv-2105-11771.title: Evaluation of Multivariate Integrals based on a Duality Identity for the Stieltjes Transform Thanks: The first author is supported by The 2022 Spirit of Ramanujan Fellowship.
arxiv-2105-11771.creator: Sarth Chavan, Christophe Vignat
arxiv-2105-11771.description: Abstract . A detailed study of a double integral representation of the Catalan’s constant allows us to identify a duality identity for the Stieltjes transform on which it is based. This duality identity is then extended to an arbitrary dimensional integral and several special cases are deduced.

arxiv-2108-13440.title: A new form of QCD coherence for multiple soft emissions using Glauber-SCET
arxiv-2108-13440.creator: Aditya Pathak
arxiv-2108-13440.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aditya Pathak. Amplitude-level factorization for a soft gluon emission has long been understood in terms of a product of loop-expanded soft-gluon currents and hard scattering matrix elements, both of which are infrared (IR) divergent. Thus, the amplitude for multiple soft gluon emissions, ordered in their relative softness, can be written as a product of IR divergent soft gluon currents and the matrix elements.

arxiv-2109-13834.title: Touchtone leakage attacks via smartphone sensors: mitigation without hardware modification
arxiv-2109-13834.creator: Connor Bolton
arxiv-2109-13834.description: Abstract Abstract Smartphone motion sensors provide a concealed mechanism for eavesdropping on acoustic information, like touchtones, emitted by a device. Eavesdropping on touchtones exposes credit card information, banking pins, and social security card numbers to malicious 3rd party apps requiring only motion sensor data.

arxiv-2207-12263.title: SecretGen: Privacy Recovery on Pre-Trained Models via Distribution Discrimination
arxiv-2207-12263.creator: Zhuowen Yuan, Fan Wu, Yunhui Long, Chaowei Xiao, Bo Li
arxiv-2207-12263.description: Abstract Transfer learning through the use of pre-trained models has become a growing trend for the machine learning community. Consequently, numerous pre-trained models are released online to facilitate further research. However, it raises extensive concerns on whether these pre-trained models would leak privacy-sensitive information of their training data.

arxiv-2301-06870.title: Learning to solve arithmetic problems with a virtual abacus
arxiv-2301-06870.creator: Flavio Petruzzellis, Ling Xuan Chen, Alberto Testolin
arxiv-2301-06870.description: Abstract Acquiring mathematical skills is considered a key challenge for modern Artificial Intelligence systems. Inspired by the way humans discover numerical knowledge, here we introduce a deep reinforcement learning framework that allows to simulate how cognitive agents could gradually learn to solve arithmetic problems by interacting with a virtual abacus.

arxiv-2305-08340.title: Efficient Semiparametric Estimation of Average Treatment Effects Under Covariate Adaptive Randomization
arxiv-2305-08340.creator: Ahnaf Rafi
arxiv-2305-08340.description: Abstract Experiments that use covariate adaptive randomization (CAR) are commonplace in applied economics and other fields. In such experiments, the experimenter first stratifies the sample according to observed baseline covariates and then assigns treatment randomly within these strata so as to achieve balance according to pre-specified stratum-specific target assignment proportions.

arxiv-2309-03554.title: Software Testing of Generative AI Systems: Challenges and Opportunities
arxiv-2309-03554.creator: Aldeida Aleti
arxiv-2309-03554.description: Abstract Software Testing is a well-established area in software engineering, encompassing various techniques and methodologies to ensure the quality and reliability of software systems. However, with the advent of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems, new challenges arise in the testing domain. These systems, capable of generating novel and creative outputs, introduce unique complexities that require novel testing approaches.

arxiv-2404-08311.title: emucxl: an emulation framework for CXL-based disaggregated memory applications
arxiv-2404-08311.creator: Raja Gond and Purushottam Kulkarni
arxiv-2404-08311.description: Abstract The emergence of CXL (Compute Express Link) promises to transform the status of interconnects between host and devices and in turn impact the design of all software layers. With its low overhead, low latency, and memory coherency capabilities, CXL has the potential to improve the performance of existing devices while making viable new operational use cases (e.g.

arxiv-2412-05384.title: Energy Correlators in Perturbative Quantum Gravity
arxiv-2412-05384.creator: Enrico Herrmann, Murat Kologlu, Ian Moult
arxiv-2412-05384.description: Abstract Despite tremendous progress in our understanding of scattering amplitudes in perturbative (super-) gravity, much less is known about other asymptotic observables, such as correlation functions of detector operators. In this paper, we initiate the study of detector operators and their correlation functions in perturbative quantum gravity.

arxiv-2502-19633.title: Empirical Discovery of Multi-Scale Transfer of Information in Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2502-19633.creator: Christopher W. Curtis, Erik M. Bollt
arxiv-2502-19633.description: Abstract In this work, we quantify the time scales and information flow associated with multiscale energy transfer in a weakly turbulent system. This is done through a greedy optimization algorithm which finds the maximum conditional-mutual information across lagged embeddings of time series localized by wavenumber.

arxiv-2510-23332.title: Quadratic Truncated Random Return in Distributional LQR: Positive Definiteness, Density, and Log-Concavity
arxiv-2510-23332.creator: Ruyi Teng, Dan Wang, Wei Chen, Yulong Gao
arxiv-2510-23332.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ruyi Teng, Dan Wang, Wei Chen, Yulong Gao. Distributional linear quadratic regulator (LQR) is a new framework that integrates the distributional reinforcement learning and classical LQR, which offers a new way to study the random return instead of the expected cost. Unlike iterative approximation using dynamic programming in the DRL, a closed-form expression for the random return can be exactly characterized in the distributional LQR, which is defined over infinitely many random variables.

arxiv-2511-14249.title: Towards Authentic Movie Dubbing with Retrieve-Augmented Director-Actor Interaction Learning
arxiv-2511-14249.creator: Rui Liu, Yuan Zhao, Zhenqi Jia
arxiv-2511-14249.description: Abstract The automatic movie dubbing model generates vivid speech from given scripts, replicating a speaker’s timbre from a brief timbre prompt while ensuring lip-sync with the silent video. Existing approaches simulate a simplified workflow where actors dub directly without preparation, overlooking the critical director–actor interaction.

cautionary-tales.title: Cautionary Tales
cautionary-tales.creator: Belloc, Hilaire
cautionary-tales.description: First published in 1907 and in print ever since, Hilaire Belloc’s Cautionary Tales for Children is a deliciously witty parody of the terribly serious moral tales for children, which were popular in Victorian times. Terrifying and funny at the same time, and with a true sense of the absurd, Belloc brings us the renowned Jim, Who ran away from his nurse, and was eaten by a Lion and unfortunate Re...

plos-pone-0005459.description: PLOS ONE research article. Young-onset hypertension has a stronger genetic component than late-onset counterpart; thus, the identification of genes related to its susceptibility is a critical issue for the prevention and management of this disease. We carried out a two-stage association scan to map young-o

pmc-11355375.title: Ad Hoc Modeling of Rate-Dependent Adhesion in Indentation Relaxation Testing
pmc-11355375.creator: Ivan I Argatov, Iakov A Lyashenko, Valentin L Popov, Ingo Dierking
pmc-11355375.description: The phenomenon of rate-dependent adhesion has long been recognized as an intricate problem, and the so-far-developed physics and mechanics-based approaches resulted in analytical relations between the implicit form between the work of adhesion and the contact front velocity which are difficult to implement in practice.

pmc-11377667.title: Metabolic alkalosis: a new red flag in status epilepticus
pmc-11377667.creator: Francesco Misirocchi, Hervé Quintard, Margitta Seeck, Pia De Stefano
pmc-11377667.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundStatus epilepticus (SE) is a heterogeneous neurological emergency with significant variability in prognosis, influenced by underlying disease and pathophysiological context. Acid–base disturbances are common in critically ill patients, yet their distribution and impact in SE patients remain poorly understood.MethodsThis was an observational cohort study including non-hypoxic SE patients with available blood gas analysis within the first 24 h of SE, treated at the University Hospital of Geneva, Switzerland between 2015 and 2023.

pmc-11386429.title: The effects of substance use on non-communicable diseases among older adults aged 60 and above in the North-eastern States of India
pmc-11386429.creator: Sasanka Boro, Nandita Saikia, Chandan Kumar, Chandan Kumar, Chandan Kumar, Chandan Kumar, Chandan Kumar
pmc-11386429.description: IntroductionThe North-eastern region of India has a relatively higher prevalence of substance use, which together with poor dietary practices and a lack of physical activity is one of the key risk factors for NCDs among older adults in the region.

pmc-11402352.title: Colonoscopic Resolution of Melanosis Coli After Cessation of Senna Laxative Use
pmc-11402352.creator: Toshimi Chiba, Ting Wang, Satoshi Kikuchi
pmc-11402352.description: Melanosis coli occurs with the administration of stimulant laxatives for the relief of constipation. However, the duration of macroscopic improvement of melanosis coli after discontinuation of anthracene laxatives is not well understood. We describe the case of an 81-year-old female diagnosed with melanosis coli via colonoscopy who had been taking senna laxatives for 5 years.

pmc-11671244.title: Serum proteome profiling of plateau acclimatization in men using Olink proteomics approach
pmc-11671244.creator: Jingyu Pan, Yue Dong, Zhihao Zou, Tianyan Gu, Ling Chen, Kai Li, Li Wang, Qinghai Shi
pmc-11671244.description: Plateau acclimatization involves adaptive changes in the body's neurohumoral regulation and metabolic processes due to hypoxic conditions at high altitudes. This study utilizes Olink targeted proteomics to analyze serum protein expression differences in Han Chinese individuals acclimatized for 6 months–1 year at 4500 and 5300 m altitudes, compared to those residing at sea level.

pmc-12636912.title: Reduction of the risk of complete sternotomy scar dehiscence in cardiac surgery: a protocol for a randomised, open-label multicentre clinical investigation comparing negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) versus standard dressing (PRISTER study)
pmc-12636912.creator: Christophe Jayle, Géraldine Allain, Amandine Buono, Simon Dang Van, Nicolas D’Ostrevy, Stéphane Kermen, Alessandro Picardo, Antoine Pelras, Julie Drux, Pierre Corbi, Maxime Billot, Denis Frasca
pmc-12636912.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionCardiac surgical procedures are associated with a high incidence of postoperative infection, a risk attributed to their inherently invasive nature and extended duration. The goal of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) compared with standard dressings in preventing sternal scar dehiscence in patients undergoing cardiac surgery via complete vertical midline sternotomy, comparing a 3 day change system (NPWT 3/7 d) versus a 7 day wear system (NPWT 7d) versus standard dressings.Methods and analysisThe PRISTER study

pmc-12795765.title: Exploring digital interaction and positive youth development in a sample of Spanish undergraduates
pmc-12795765.creator: Esther López-Bermúdez, Gina Tomé, Diego Gómez-Baya
pmc-12795765.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study examined the associations between different types of internet use and Positive Youth Development (PYD) among Spanish university students, considering gender differences. A total of 1779 undergraduate students (65.9% men, M age = 20.32, SD = 1.84) from ten universities in Andalusia (Spain) completed online self-report measures assessing the five dimensions of PYD and some internet use behaviors, including social networking, online gaming, reading, surfing or looking for information, music-related activities, and e-commerce.

pmc-13038456.title: Serum neurofilament light chain in hydrocephalus and surgical controls: baseline comparison and 24-hour perioperative dynamics under general anesthesia
pmc-13038456.creator: Miroslav Cihlo, Pavel Trávníček, Alena Tichá, Radomír Hyšpler, Marta Kalousová, Tomáš Česák, Karel Zadrobílek, Lucie Kukrálová, Pavel Dostál, Tomáš Zima, Michaela Sluková, Vlasta Dostálová
pmc-13038456.description: Background/Objectives neurofilament light chain (NfL) is a blood-accessible marker of neuroaxonal injury. We assessed the clinical utility of serum NfL in adults with idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH). Methods in a single-center prospective cohort (registered at ClinicalTrials.gov; partial overlap with a prior registry detailed in Supplementary Table S1), we enrolled 41 adults aged ≥ 50 years.

pmc-13097802.title: Ischemic stroke during dengue–Plasmodium vivax coinfection in a young woman: a case report
pmc-13097802.creator: H A Nati-Castillo, Jhan S Saavedra-Torres, José Mauricio Cardenas, Alice Gaibor-Pazmiño, Esteban Ortiz-Prado, Juan S Izquierdo-Condoy
pmc-13097802.description: BackgroundMalaria and dengue are tropical endemic infections that can cause severe vascular and neurologic complications. Coinfection with Plasmodium vivax and dengue virus is uncommon but increasingly reported in co-endemic areas, complicating diagnosis and suggesting possible pathogenic synergy. Although each pathogen has been linked to stroke, cerebrovascular events during coinfection are exceptionally rare.
